title: Beylik of Menteshe
capsule: The Beylik of Menteshe was a Turkmen principality founded around 1261 by Menteshe Bey in southwestern Anatolia, roughly coinciding with ancient Caria and modern Muğla Province. It distinguished itself as the first seafaring Anatolian beylik, seizing a portion of Rhodes around 1300 and extracting tribute from Aegean islands after 1332, while trading grain, horses, and alum with Venetian Crete from its chief ports at Milas and Balat. A severe earthquake in 1389 weakened the polity, and Bayezid I absorbed it into the Ottoman state in 1390; Timur briefly restored it after 1402, placing Ilyas Bey on the throne, but the Ottomans re-annexed it permanently by 1426. Its territory is now Muğla Province in Turkey.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Menteshe in Muğla Province is well-attested; the precise boundaries with neighboring beyliks (Aydın, Germiyan) fluctuated and are only approximately charted.
